rows.name: Breadbelly
rows.why: Taiwanese-style fried chicken, sharp pickles and house milk bread.

rows.name: Lily
rows.why: The Chronicle singled out this sandwich inspired by Hanoi’s turmeric fish.

rows.name: Lou’s Cafe
rows.why: Melted Swiss and cheddar, avocado and jalapeño spread balance heat and richness.
rows.lunch: Daily at lunchtime; opens at 8 a.m. Mon–Sat and 9 a.m. Sun.

rows.name: Burma Superstar
rows.why: The fermented tea leaves and crunchy toppings are the draw; add the coconut chicken noodles for a full lunch.
rows.order: Tea leaf salad and coconut chicken noodle soup
rows.lunch: Dine-in: Mon–Thu 11:30 a.m.–2:30 p.m.; Fri–Sun 11:30 a.m.–3 p.m.

rows.name: Nippon Curry
rows.why: Crisp breaded prawns with a rich Japanese curry and rice. A quick savory lunch option.
rows.lunch: Weekdays 11 a.m.–2 p.m. (earlier opening Wed); weekends from 11 a.m.

rows.name: Causwells
rows.why: The double smashburger with American cheese, pickles and house sauce is the standout dish.
rows.lunch: Tue–Fri from 11 a.m.; Sat–Sun from 10 a.m. Closed Mon.

rows.name: Côte Ouest Bistro
rows.why: Crisp duck leg with potato gratin and wild mushroom sauce on the weekday lunch menu.
rows.lunch: Tue–Fri 11:30 a.m.–2:30 p.m. for this lunch menu.

rows.name: Mandalay
rows.why: The James Beard Foundation called out both dishes: coconut chicken flat noodles and a tangy lentil-and-samusa soup.
rows.order: Mandalay Special Noodle and samusa soup
rows.lunch: Fri–Sun 11:30 a.m.–3 p.m. No Mon–Thu lunch.

rows.name: A16
rows.why: A classic wood-fired Neapolitan pie. The Michelin Guide singles out the pizza.
rows.lunch: Fri–Sun from noon. No Mon–Thu lunch.

rows.name: Deli Board
rows.why: Hot pastrami, sauerkraut, Swiss and cherry peppers make for a different kind of deli sandwich.
rows.lunch: Tue–Sun 11 a.m.–3 p.m.; last order 2:50 p.m. or earlier at capacity. Takeout.

rows.name: Dumpling Home
rows.why: The soup dumplings are a strong reason to go. Add Juicy Pork Bao if you want a pan-fried second order.
rows.order: Numb & Spicy Pork Xiao Long Bao

rows.name: Hook Fish Co.
rows.why: The fish changes with the catch. The Infatuation calls out the burrito as an order to get.

rows.name: Beit Rima
rows.why: Yogurt-marinated chicken with toum, hummus, rice and pita is a full lunch.

rows.name: La Taqueria
rows.why: Ask for dorado for a crisp outer tortilla. A Mission stop singled out by the Michelin Guide.

source.label: Reviewed lunch menus, business hours, and independent food coverage
caveats: Menus and published lunch hours checked 2026-11-09. Service and dishes can change.
Recommendations are editorial and do not imply a personal visit or rating.

rows.name: Southeast Community Center
rows.why: The city provides public workspaces and free Wi-Fi here. Hungry Cafe was set up with remote workers in mind.
rows.summary: Free public workspaces with an on-site café
rows.wifi: Free Wi-Fi confirmed by SFPUC. Outlets reported by a work guide.
rows.tip: The community center opens earlier and closes later than Hungry Cafe, which posts weekday hours of 8 a.m.–4 p.m.
rows.hours: Public access Mon–Fri 7 a.m.–7 p.m.
rows.trial: Try a weekday at 10 a.m. See whether you can find a powered table away from the café counter.

rows.name: 101 Second Street Atrium
rows.why: The local community benefit district reports that people use laptops in this publicly accessible greenhouse atrium.
rows.summary: Public indoor atrium with a mezzanine
rows.wifi: One visitor reports spotty Wi-Fi and some outlets. Bring a hotspot or work offline.
rows.tip: Enter near Second and Mission. Try before the office lunch rush.
rows.hours: Listed Mon–Fri 8 a.m.–6 p.m.
rows.trial: See whether the mezzanine has a free table and enough reception for an hour of work.

rows.name: Sōhn
rows.why: A firsthand work guide reports Wi-Fi, laptop use and seating on both levels.
rows.summary: Two floors for a laptop session
rows.wifi: Wi-Fi reported. Outlet access is unconfirmed.
rows.tip: Start upstairs on a weekday and pick a time outside the lunch rush.
rows.hours: Tue–Sun 9 a.m.–4 p.m., closed Mon
rows.trial: Try 1:30 p.m. on a weekday and see whether the upstairs tables stay conversational.

rows.name: Progressive Grounds
rows.why: A firsthand work guide describes indoor tables, a roomy patio and people settling in with laptops.
rows.summary: Neighborhood café with a back patio
rows.wifi: Free Wi-Fi reported. Outlet access is unconfirmed.
rows.tip: The patio is an option on a dry day. Monday closes earlier.
rows.hours: Listed Mon 6:30 a.m.–3 p.m., Tue–Fri 6:30 a.m.–6 p.m., weekends 7 a.m.–6 p.m.
rows.trial: Try the patio on a weekday and check whether the Wi-Fi reaches the back tables.

rows.name: Paris Cafe
rows.why: The café invites laptop work and study and describes space for solo visitors and groups.
rows.summary: Roomy tables with a published laptop policy
rows.wifi: The operator advertises fast Wi-Fi. Outlet access is unconfirmed.
rows.tip: Use the weekday hours as a starting point. Check directly for weekend hours, which differ across listings.
rows.hours: Mon–Fri 7 a.m.–6 p.m. Check weekends.
rows.trial: Try midafternoon and see whether a solo table is easy to find when groups are there.

rows.name: Fiddle Fig Cafe
rows.why: A firsthand work guide reports plenty of seating and Wi-Fi at this sunny corner café.
rows.summary: Roomy neighborhood café with Wi-Fi
rows.wifi: Wi-Fi reported. Outlet access is unconfirmed.
rows.tip: Bring a charged laptop and try a weekday away from lunch.
rows.hours: Listed daily 8 a.m.–4 p.m.
rows.trial: Check whether there are open tables and enough quiet for an hour around 2 p.m.

rows.name: Beluna Café
rows.why: A firsthand review reports plenty of seating, fast Wi-Fi and a low hum of conversation. Try the upstairs mezzanine.
rows.summary: Upstairs tables and plenty of plugs
rows.wifi: Fast Wi-Fi and outlets reported.
rows.tip: Try a weekday morning. Weekend seats can fill.
rows.hours: Listed daily 8 a.m.–3 p.m.

rows.name: Sacred Grounds Café
rows.why: The café explicitly welcomes work and study and describes several seating nooks.
rows.summary: Neighborhood café that welcomes laptops
rows.wifi: Free Wi-Fi confirmed by the café.
rows.tip: Try a weekday. The café says weekend mornings are its busiest.
rows.hours: Weekdays 8 a.m.–3 p.m.; weekends 9 a.m.–3 p.m.

rows.name: Atlas Café
rows.why: A work guide recommends the spacious room and patio for laptop time. A good fit if you want food with your coffee.
rows.summary: Laptop tables and a back patio
rows.wifi: Wi-Fi reported; outlets unverified.
rows.tip: Aim for a weekday morning before the lunch crowd.
rows.hours: Mon–Fri 7 a.m.–6 p.m.; Sat 8 a.m.–6 p.m.; Sun 8 a.m.–4 p.m.

rows.name: Another Cafe
rows.why: The café welcomes work and study, and a remote worker reports finding afternoon seating with reliable Wi-Fi.
rows.summary: Laptop-friendly and open until 8
rows.wifi: Wi-Fi and some outlets reported.
rows.tip: A later option when most cafés have closed. Expect some conversation.
rows.hours: Daily 7 a.m.–8 p.m.

rows.name: Ocean Beach Cafe
rows.why: The work guide reports Wi-Fi and plenty of bar and table seating.
rows.summary: Roomy café for a weekday session
rows.wifi: Wi-Fi reported; outlets unverified.
rows.tip: Go on a weekday. The Saturday 10 a.m. run club can make it busier.
rows.hours: Mon–Thu 8 a.m.–5 p.m.; Fri–Sun 8 a.m.–6 p.m.

rows.name: Sports Basement · Sign Room
rows.why: An enclosed community room at the Presidio store, with tables, a TV and power.
rows.summary: Free reservable room for up to 30
rows.wifi: Wi-Fi and outlets confirmed by Sports Basement.
rows.tip: Reserve ahead and review the community-use guidelines for your meeting.
rows.hours: Room hours Mon–Fri 10 a.m.–8 p.m., Sat–Sun 9 a.m.–7 p.m.

room.details: Free with reservation. Up to 30 seated theater-style, with four tables.

rows.name: Trellis
rows.why: Work in the public café, or reserve an enclosed room or sound-isolated booth for a call.
rows.summary: Public café, group rooms and a solo call booth
rows.wifi: Coworking Wi-Fi is advertised. Check café coverage at your table.
rows.tip: The public café is open weekdays 9 a.m.–4 p.m. Book the booth separately if you only need space for one person.
rows.hours: Coworking Mon–Fri 9 a.m.–5 p.m.

room.details: Dahlia seats six. See checkout for the room rate. Separate solo booth is $10/hr.

rows.name: Pacific Workplaces Downtown
rows.why: A practical small-room option with online booking, on-site staff and fast Wi-Fi.
rows.summary: Three-person office or four-person conference room
rows.wifi: The operator lists fiber Wi-Fi in its meeting spaces.
rows.tip: Nonmembers can reserve online. Choose the day office for a small meeting or private call.
rows.hours: By appointment. Check the booking calendar.

room.details: Three-seat day office $30/hr. Four-seat conference room $60/hr. One-hour minimum.

rows.name: CANOPY Pacific Heights
rows.why: A small enclosed conference room and a larger boardroom. Both have presentation equipment.
rows.summary: Five-person room on Fillmore
rows.wifi: Check the booking page for room amenities.
rows.tip: Nonmembers can book by the hour or day. Choose Pacific Heights when looking up times.
rows.hours: Check the booking calendar for room times.

room.details: Conference room seats five. Boardroom seats eight. Rates in the booking calendar.

rows.name: Carr Workplaces Embarcadero
rows.why: The Lombard room has a display and a whiteboard. A day office is also available for one or two people.
rows.summary: Five-person meeting room near the waterfront
rows.wifi: Wi-Fi listed for the conference room and day office.
rows.tip: Use the Plan Your Meeting form to ask about openings. The nonmember meeting-room terms list a two-hour minimum.
rows.hours: Business hours 8:30 a.m.–5 p.m. Confirm room times.

room.details: Lombard room for five at $75/hr. Day office for one or two at $50/hr. Nonmember rates.

rows.name: Richmond Branch Library
rows.why: A free walk-in option for focused laptop time, with a large reading room and two first-come study rooms.
rows.summary: Large reading room with tables
rows.wifi: Free SFPL Wi-Fi.
rows.tip: Ask at the desk about a study room; take calls elsewhere. Check for holiday closures.
rows.hours: Mon/Sat 10 a.m.–6 p.m.; Tue–Thu 10 a.m.–8 p.m.; Fri 1–6 p.m.; Sun 1–5 p.m.

rows.name: West Portal Branch Library
rows.why: The branch has reading rooms with restored tables and chairs, a practical spot for solo work.
rows.summary: Reading tables and task lighting
rows.wifi: Free SFPL Wi-Fi.
rows.tip: Free walk-in. Take calls elsewhere and check holiday hours.
rows.hours: Mon/Sat 10 a.m.–6 p.m.; Tue–Thu 10 a.m.–8 p.m.; Fri 1–6 p.m.; Sun 1–5 p.m.

rows.name: Mission Bay Branch Library
rows.why: A free indoor option for focused work with study tables and two first-come study rooms.
rows.summary: Study tables and short-use study rooms
rows.wifi: Free SFPL Wi-Fi.
rows.tip: Study rooms hold up to two people and are intended for hour-long sessions. Check holiday hours.
rows.hours: Mon/Tue/Thu/Sat 10 a.m.–6 p.m.; Wed 11 a.m.–8 p.m.; Fri 1–6 p.m.; Sun 1–5 p.m.

rows.name: Glen Park Branch Library
rows.why: A neighborhood branch with reported window-side seating, useful for reading or laptop work near Glen Park BART.
rows.summary: Window-side seats near BART
rows.wifi: Free SFPL Wi-Fi.
rows.tip: Check the branch calendar if you want to avoid storytime or group events.
rows.hours: Mon/Tue/Sat 10 a.m.–6 p.m.; Wed noon–8 p.m.; Thu 10 a.m.–7 p.m.; Fri 1–6 p.m.; Sun 1–5 p.m.

source.label: Published hours, Wi-Fi information, and reports on working there
caveats: Sources checked 2026-11-09; holiday hours and café policies can change.
Crowds vary. Room listings show booking options and published terms. Check the operator for live openings.
Worth testing marks an unconfirmed detail to check during a visit.
